theory.title: CPPI Invariant Wealth Floor & Safety Buffer Derivation
theory.summary: Proves why the buffered trigger P_floor = max(P_liq/(1-γ), (F-c)/(n(1-γ))) guarantees V ≥ F and a complete exit before the market reaches P_liq.

tech.title: Floor & Safety Buffer State Kernel
tech.summary: Exact float64 computation of p_floor and safety_buf_usd, and why the intra-bar low[t] <= p_floor check runs before anything else.

theory.title: Whipsaw Decay as Dynamic Put Replication Cost
theory.summary: Shows how selling low and rebuying higher shrinks the recoverable inventory n_max, raises the safety buffer, and is bounded by the cushion.

tech.title: Cushion & Recoverable BTC Accounting
tech.summary: How n_max, the cushion and the cumulative fee and slippage bleed are computed, and the rebuy cap that keeps a purchase cushion-funded.

theory.title: Dual-Envelope Control Law & Hysteresis Deadband
theory.summary: Derives the sell ceiling and rebuy floor from the normalised distance d and shows why the band between them prevents fee churn.

tech.title: Envelope Evaluation & Minimum Rebalance Quantum
tech.summary: Evaluation order of d, n_ceil and n_floor at the bar close, the Δn_min filter and the near-floor override inside the final 250 USD.

theory.title: Continuous Risk-Aversion (ρ) & Urgency Escalation Theory
theory.summary: Formulates the trade-off between the maker fee saving and the exposure created by a missed fill, and how urgency escalates an order to taker.

tech.title: Order Routing Engine (route_order_by_rho)
tech.summary: Exact branching for ρ = 0, 0 < ρ < 1 and ρ = 1, the miss counter m_miss, and the maker-dominance guard.

theory.title: Stochastic Order-Book Liquidity & Pass-Through Theory
theory.summary: Derives the three-factor fill probability P_fill = Φ_pen · Φ_vel · Φ_size and the Bernoulli resolution against a uniform variate.

tech.title: Stochastic Fill Sampler & PCG64 Seeding
tech.summary: Implementation of λ_liq, β_vel and α_size, the per-bar PCG64 uniform vector, and the parallel Monte Carlo ensemble.

theory.title: Asymmetric Decline (S_down) & Growth (S_up) Microstructure Signals
theory.summary: Explains volatility-normalised EMA momentum, taker-flow imbalance, range breakout and the crash-veto gate.

tech.title: Vectorized Signal Pipeline
tech.summary: The O(T) array passes for EMA, ATR, rolling sums and extrema, the CLV volume fallback, and the conventions at the start of a window.

theory.title: Discrete-Time Execution Model, Event Ordering & Gap Risk
theory.summary: Why the five steps of a bar run in that order, what a 1-minute bar can and cannot guarantee, and the one case in which V can end below F.

tech.title: Numba State-Machine Loop & Telemetry Schema
tech.summary: The compiled loop step by step, the 26-field telemetry row, event priority within a bar, and the floating-point guards.

theory.title: Reading the Experiment: Market Data, Rescaling, KPIs & the Monte Carlo Fan
theory.summary: What the bundled data is, what price rescaling preserves, how to read the eight KPI cards and what the 5-95 % fan does and does not say.

tech.title: Data Engine, Recalculation Pipeline & UI Event Bindings
tech.summary: Parquet schema and importers, the cached recalculation pipeline and its latency, the chart renderer, the ledger model and the popover timers.

param-start.title: Start Date & Time (UTC) — $t_0$
param-start.summary: First bar of the back-test window. The simulation covers every bar with $t_0 \le \tau_t < t_0 + \Delta T$ of the active dataset.
details: Range: the first to the last bar of the active dataset, in 1-minute steps.
Signals are computed on the selected window only, so two windows that overlap do not share warm-up history.
param-start.implementation: MarketData.window() slices the dataset arrays without copying; the controller caches the slice until the start, duration or rescaling changes.

param-duration.title: Simulation Duration — $\Delta T$
param-duration.summary: Length of the back-test in days. Thirty days of 1-minute bars is 43,200 bars.
details: Range 1 to 365 days in 1-day steps.
A window that runs past the end of the dataset is simply shorter; the bar count in the top bar is the truth.
param-duration.implementation: Longer windows only cost time linearly: the kernel is $O(T)$ and the chart never draws more than two points per pixel.

param-n0.title: Initial BTC Holdings — $N_0$
param-n0.summary: BTC held at the first bar. Together with $c_0$ and $P_{\text{liq}}$ it fixes the hard floor.
details: Range 0.001 to 1000 BTC, step 0.05.
The minimum rebalance quantum is a percentage of $N_0$, so order sizes scale with the account.
Larger orders face a lower $\Phi_{\text{size}}$: a 100 BTC resting order needs 100 times the counter-party volume of a 1 BTC order.
param-n0.implementation: Equity is plotted as $V_t / N_0$ so it shares the price axis whatever the account size.

param-c0.title: Initial USD Cash — $c_0$
param-c0.summary: USD held at the first bar. It is part of the protected wealth and is also deployable: the envelope may spend it on BTC when the growth signal allows.
details: Range 0 to 10,000,000 USD, step 100 USD.
param-c0.implementation: Cash enters the recoverable inventory $n_{\max,t} = n_t + c_t / (P_t(1+f_{\text{eff}}))$ from the first bar.

param-normalize.title: Normalize Start Price to Reference Anchor
param-normalize.summary: Multiplies every open, high, low and close of the window by one factor so the first open equals the anchor price. Use it to replay a historical crash as if it had started just above your floor.
param-normalize.math: \kappa = \frac{P_{\text{anchor}}}{O_0}, \qquad (O_t, H_t, L_t, C_t) \mapsto \kappa \, (O_t, H_t, L_t, C_t)
details: Percentage returns, volatility clustering and the taker-flow imbalance are preserved exactly; volumes stay in BTC and are not touched.
Absolute USD constants of the model (the 1 USD ATR floor, the 250 USD near-floor zone) are not rescaled, so a window rescaled by a large factor is a stress test, not a replay.
While it is on, the top bar shows the factor $\kappa$ in an amber chip so rescaled prices are never mistaken for history.
param-normalize.implementation: MarketWindow.rescaled() returns new price arrays and reuses the volume arrays; the raw dataset is never modified.

param-p-liq.title: Hard Liquidation Floor Price — $P_{\text{liq}}$
param-p-liq.summary: The price below which the account must hold no BTC. The strategy guarantees a complete sale before the market trades below it, on every bar that does not gap.
details: Range 1,000 to 250,000 USD, step 250 USD.
The emergency sale is triggered at $P_{\text{floor},t}$, not at $P_{\text{liq}}$: the gap between them pays the taker fee and slippage of the exit.
Raising $P_{\text{liq}}$ raises the floor value $F$ and pushes $P_{\text{ref}}$ up if it would otherwise sit less than 1,000 USD above it.

param-p-ref.title: Upper Full-Allocation Reference — $P_{\text{ref}}$
param-p-ref.summary: The price at and above which the envelope allows full allocation. Between the trigger and $P_{\text{ref}}$ the permitted holding grows linearly.
details: Range $P_{\text{liq}} + 1{,}000$ USD to 350,000 USD, step 500 USD.
A narrow band makes $d_t$ steep: small price moves produce large rebalances.
Above $P_{\text{ref}}$ the ceiling equals $n_{\max}$, so no sell is ever requested there.

param-dn-min.title: Minimum Rebalance Threshold — $\Delta n_{\min}$
param-dn-min.summary: The smallest order the control law will place, as a percentage of $N_0$. It is the width of the dead zone around each envelope edge and the main lever against fee churn.
details: Range 0.1 % to 25 %, step 0.25 %.
Sells inside the last 250 USD above the trigger ignore it, so the position can always be reduced to zero.
Buys always respect it; a purchase the rebuy cap would shrink below it is not placed.

param-f-maker.title: Maker Fee Rate — $f_{\text{maker}}$
param-f-maker.summary: Fee paid on a passive post_only order that fills at its limit price.
details: Range 0 % to 1 %, step 0.01 %.
Enters the blended conversion rate $f_{\text{eff}}(\rho) = (1-\rho) f_{\text{maker}} + \rho f_{\text{taker}}$ used for $n_{\max}$.
If $f_{\text{maker}} \ge f_{\text{taker}} + \delta_{\text{slip}}$ a passive order is dearer than an immediate one and uncertain as well; the router then sends every order as a taker.

param-f-taker.title: Taker Fee Rate — $f_{\text{taker}}$
param-f-taker.summary: Fee paid on an order that executes immediately. With the slippage allowance it forms the emergency exit friction $\gamma$.
details: Range 0 % to 2 %, step 0.01 %.
A larger $\gamma$ lifts the baseline trigger $P_{\text{liq}}/(1-\gamma)$ and lowers the liquidation value $V_t = c_t + n_t P_t (1-\gamma)$.
param-f-taker.implementation: Taker frictions are additive, exactly as in the emergency formula of TSD §3.1: a sale nets $q P (1-\gamma)$ and a purchase costs $q P (1+\gamma)$.

param-delta-slip.title: Safety Buffer Slippage Allowance — $\delta_{\text{slip}}$
param-delta-slip.summary: Price concession assumed on every immediate order, and the slippage reserved inside the safety buffer for the emergency exit.
details: Range 0 % to 2 %, step 0.01 %.
At the defaults $\gamma = 0.40\,\%$ and the baseline buffer is 240.96 USD above a 60,000 USD floor.

param-rho.title: Risk-Aversion Parameter — $\rho \in [0, 1]$
param-rho.summary: Tunes how conservatively the strategy chooses between passive post_only maker orders (lower fee, stochastic fill probability $P_{\text{fill},t}$) and immediate taker orders (higher fee, guaranteed fill).
details: $\rho = 0$: places only passive maker orders above the buffered floor, and only places a taker sell order when the liquidation level + safety buffer $P_{\text{floor},t}$ is reached (the realised sell price after slippage lands below $P_{\text{floor},t}$ but at or above $P_{\text{liq}}$).
$\rho = 1$: places only immediate taker orders for every buy and sell rebalance.
$0 < \rho < 1$: splits the order ($\rho$ taker, $1-\rho$ maker) and escalates to 100 % taker whenever the execution urgency $u_t \ge 1 - \rho$.
param-rho.implementation: route_order_by_rho in engine/kernel_numba.py; the miss counter $m_{\text{miss}}$ feeds the urgency.

param-lambda-liq.title: Base Liquidity Depth Factor — $\lambda_{\text{liq}}$
param-lambda-liq.summary: How quickly the chance of a fill rises as the bar trades further through the limit price. It models the depth of the queue ahead of the order.
details: Range 0.10 to 10, step 0.10.
$\Delta P_{\text{pen}}$ is how far the bar's high (sell) or low (buy) went beyond the limit. A touch without penetration never fills.

param-beta-vel.title: Adverse Price Velocity Penalty — $\beta_{\text{vel}}$
param-beta-vel.summary: Penalises bars that swept away from the resting order: a sell limit is unlikely to fill in a bar that closed far below its open.
details: Range 0 to 10, step 0.10. For a buy the numerator is $\max(0, C_t - O_t)$.
This is the factor that makes maker sells fail exactly when they matter most, in a fast decline.

param-alpha-size.title: Order Size Impact Exponent — $\alpha_{\text{size}}$
param-alpha-size.summary: How sharply the fill probability falls once the order is large relative to the opposing taker volume of the bar.
details: Range 0.10 to 5, step 0.10.
$V_{\text{opp}}$ is buyer-taker volume for a resting sell and seller-taker volume for a resting buy; one per cent of it is taken as absorbable.

param-seed.title: Uniform PRNG Seed — $s_{\text{rng}}$
param-seed.summary: Seed of the uniform variates that decide every maker fill. The same seed always reproduces the same trajectory, on any machine.
param-seed.math: U_t \le P_{\text{fill},t} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{fill at the limit}, \qquad U_t > P_{\text{fill},t} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{missed order}
details: One variate is drawn per bar and indexed by bar, so changing a strategy parameter does not reshuffle the randomness: sensitivity tests compare like with like.
param-seed.implementation: np.random.Generator(np.random.PCG64(s_rng)).random(T), generated once per (seed, window length) and cached.

param-mc-fan.title: Monte Carlo Liquidity Fan — $M = 100$ Seeds
param-mc-fan.summary: Runs the back-test for one hundred seeds in parallel and shades the 5th to 95th percentile of net equity behind the active trajectory. The width of the band is the part of the outcome that is luck of the fill.
details: Member $m$ uses seed $s_{\text{rng}} + m$, so member 0 is exactly the trajectory on screen.
At $\rho = 1$ nothing is stochastic and the fan collapses onto the line.
The Floor Integrity card reports conservation breaches and liquidations across all one hundred members.
param-mc-fan.implementation: engine/monte_carlo.py: the same compiled kernel inside a prange loop, run on a worker thread so the controls stay responsive.

param-ema-d.title: Decline Signal: Fast / Slow EMA Windows — $W_{f,d},\ W_{s,d}$
param-ema-d.summary: Spans of the two exponential averages of the close whose difference measures downward momentum.
details: Fast 1 to 60 minutes, slow 10 to 240 minutes, step 1 minute.
Shorter windows react sooner and flicker more; every flicker moves the sell ceiling.

param-atr-d.title: Decline Signal: Volatility ATR Window — $W_{\text{atr},d}$
param-atr-d.summary: Span of the average true range that normalises downward momentum. The same ATR is the volatility yardstick of the fill model.
details: Range 5 to 120 minutes, step 1 minute.

param-imb-d.title: Decline Signal: Trade Flow Imbalance Window — $W_{\text{imb},d}$
param-imb-d.summary: Number of bars over which taker sell volume is compared with taker buy volume.
details: Range 2 to 60 minutes, step 1 minute.
The imbalance saturates at 1 when sellers account for 70 % of taker volume.

param-w-mom-d.title: Momentum vs. Imbalance Weight — $w_{m,d}$
param-w-mom-d.summary: Blend between price momentum and order-flow imbalance in the decline signal.
details: Range 0 to 1, step 0.05. At 1 the signal is pure momentum, at 0 pure flow.

param-k-sell.title: Decline Signal Gain — $k_{\text{sell}}$
param-k-sell.summary: How strongly the decline signal pulls the sell ceiling below the linear glidepath.
details: Range 0.10 to 2, step 0.05.
The effect is largest half-way down the band and vanishes at both ends, where $d_t(1-d_t) = 0$.
Above 1 the bracket can turn negative; it is floored at zero, so the ceiling never goes below zero.

param-ema-u.title: Growth Signal: Fast / Slow EMA Windows — $W_{f,u},\ W_{s,u}$
param-ema-u.summary: Spans of the two averages whose difference measures the upward trend. They are deliberately slower than the decline pair: selling should be quick, rebuying patient.
details: Fast 5 to 120 minutes, slow 30 to 480 minutes, step 5 minutes.

param-atr-u.title: Growth Signal: Volatility ATR Window — $W_{\text{atr},u}$
param-atr-u.summary: Span of the average true range that normalises the upward trend.
details: Range 15 to 240 minutes, step 5 minutes.

param-brk-u.title: Growth Signal: Range Breakout Window — $W_{\text{brk},u}$
param-brk-u.summary: Look-back of the high-low range. The breakout term is positive only while the close is in the upper half of that range.
param-brk-u.math: B_{\text{up},t} = \operatorname{clip}\!\left(\frac{C_t - M_t}{R_t},\,0,\,1\right), \quad M_t = \tfrac12\big(H^{(W)}_t + L^{(W)}_t\big),\ R_t = \max\!\big(\tfrac12(H^{(W)}_t - L^{(W)}_t),\,1\big)
details: Range 30 to 1,440 minutes, step 15 minutes.

param-tau-veto.title: Decline Veto Gate Threshold — $\tau_{\text{veto}}$
param-tau-veto.summary: Level of the decline signal at which rebuying is switched off completely. Below it the growth signal is scaled down linearly.
details: Range 0.10 to 1, step 0.05.
Independently of the gate, the control law never buys while $S_{\text{down},t} \ge 0.25$.

kpi-equity.title: Net Equity — $V_T$
kpi-equity.summary: Liquidation value of the account at the last bar: cash plus BTC valued at the close, net of the fee and slippage an immediate exit would cost.
details: The subtitle compares it with $V_0$, the same quantity at the first bar.
Because it is net of exit friction, a full position shows $V_t$ about $\gamma$ below its mark-to-market value.

kpi-cushion.title: Active Risk Cushion — $C_T = \max(0, V_T - F)$
kpi-cushion.summary: What the account can still lose before it is worth only the floor. Every whipsaw and every fee is paid out of it; when it reaches zero the strategy can no longer hold BTC.
details: The subtitle is the smallest value of $V_t - F$ seen during the run.

kpi-floor.title: Floor Integrity
kpi-floor.summary: The conservation assertion of the strategy: $V_t \ge F - 10^{-6}$ on every bar that did not gap. It is counted inside the simulation kernel, not inferred afterwards.
details: INTACT: the trigger was never reached.
LIQUIDATED: the emergency exit fired at the trigger and the proceeds were at least $F$.
GAP BREACH: a bar opened below the trigger, so the exit could only be executed at the open. This is the one case the model does not protect against, and the shortfall is shown.
With the Monte Carlo fan on, the subtitle reports breaches and liquidations across all 100 seeds.

kpi-holdings.title: BTC Held — $n_T$
kpi-holdings.summary: BTC in the account at the last bar. The subtitle is the recoverable inventory: what the account would hold if all its cash were converted back at the last close.
details: $n_{\max}$ below $N_0$ after a round trip is whipsaw decay measured in BTC.

kpi-trigger.title: Liquidation Trigger — $P_{\text{floor},T}$
kpi-trigger.summary: Price at which the emergency taker exit would fire at the last bar: the liquidation level plus the safety buffer.
details: It turns amber once the buffer is more than twice its baseline, a sign that realised whipsaw has lifted the trigger.

kpi-fills.title: Fills — Maker / Taker
kpi-fills.summary: Number of executed orders by route. The subtitle is the share of traded BTC that went through passive orders.
details: Emergency liquidations are taker executions but are counted on the Floor Integrity card, not here.
Raise $\rho$ and the taker share rises, together with the fee bill and the certainty of execution.

kpi-missed.title: Missed Maker Orders
kpi-missed.summary: Passive orders whose limit was reached or crossed but which did not fill because $U_t > P_{\text{fill},t}$, or that the bar never traded through.
details: A missed sell in a falling market is the cost of saving the taker fee: the position stays on while the price moves away.
Each miss raises the urgency of the next order through $m_{\text{miss}}$.

kpi-costs.title: Fees + Slippage Paid
kpi-costs.summary: Everything execution has cost: maker fees, taker fees and the slippage allowance on every immediate order, including the emergency exit.
details: The subtitle expresses it as a share of the starting equity.
It is a lower bound on whipsaw decay; selling low and rebuying higher adds a price loss on top.

pane-price.title: Pane 1 — Price, Floor & Net Portfolio Equity
pane-price.summary: The market and the account on one axis. Net equity is drawn per initial BTC, $V_t / N_0$, so it can be read against the price.
details: White line and grey band: close and the low-high range of each bar.
Red dashed line: $P_{\text{liq}}$. Orange stepped line and shaded zone: the trigger $P_{\text{floor},t}$ and the safety buffer.
Markers: ▼ maker sell, ▲ maker buy, ◆ taker sell (with stem) and taker buy, ○ missed maker order; a full-height red line is a hard-buffer liquidation.
Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, double-click to zoom out, click to select a bar in the ledger.

pane-holdings.title: Pane 2 — BTC Holdings & Hysteresis Deadband
pane-holdings.summary: What the strategy holds against what it is allowed to hold. No order is placed while the yellow line stays inside the shaded band.
details: Yellow steps: BTC held. Grey: recoverable inventory $n_{\max}$.
Pink dashes: the sell ceiling. Green dashes: the rebuy floor. Shading: the no-trade deadband.
When several bars share a pixel the envelope edges are drawn as bucket averages, so a fast-flickering signal does not paint the pane solid.

pane-signals.title: Pane 3 — Signals & Fill Probability Diagnostics
pane-signals.summary: The two inputs of the control law and the coin flip behind every maker order.
details: Red area: decline signal $S_{\text{down}}$. Green area: growth signal $S_{\text{up}}$.

Each purple stem is one maker order attempt and rises to its fill probability. The dot is the uniform draw: a solid purple dot at or below the top of the stem is a fill, a hollow amber ring above it is a miss.
